source_evidence: Investors in hedge funds typically pay an asset management fee of 1-2% of NAV. In addition, they also typically pay a performance fee of 15-20% of the hedge fund’s profit subject to certain measures, such as a high-water mark and a hurdle rate, which can limit when a manager is entitled to performance fees.
question: Misconception: A hedge fund’s performance fee is simply a fee charged on all the fund’s assets, just like its management fee.
answer: A hedge fund’s management fee is typically based on NAV, while its performance fee is typically based on the fund’s profit. The performance fee may also be subject to measures such as a high-water mark or hurdle rate, which can limit when the manager is entitled to collect it.
